extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors/reviewers/recommenders in mathematical & computational biology submitting preprints to PCI Math & Comp Biol
extracted.subtask_short: submitting preprints to PCI Math & Comp Biol
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and platform-level requirements for submitting a preprint to the Peer Community In (PCI) Mathematical & Computational Biology community, and for participating as a reviewer or recommender. Covers required metadata, mandatory pre-submission readings, licensing, and possible publication outcomes for recommended preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission metadata fields (required/optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission form fields shown on the site include: Id; Title *; Authors *; Year *; Abstract *; Keywords (optional); Methods that require specific expertise (optional); Thematic fields *; Submission date; Recommender; Reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asterisks indicate mandatory fields. Authors must supply the required metadata (title, authors, year, abstract, thematic fields) when submitting a preprint. Optional fields such as keywords and methods-requiring-specific-expertise can be provided to help classification and reviewer selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission reading / compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting a preprint, authors are instructed to 'please carefully read the guide for authors, PCI Math & Comp Biol's community-developed editorial policies, and find out what you can do with a PCI Math & Comp Biol-recommended preprint.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the Guide for Authors and the community-developed editorial policies and comply with any formatting, scope, ethical, and procedural requirements described there. The site repeatedly points authors/recommenders/reviewers to their respective guides (Guide for Reviewers, Guide for Recommenders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted article types / scope statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The site states: 'We accept most types of articles.' It is a peer-review platform for preprints in the field of Mathematical and Computational Biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although broadly accepting most article types, authors should verify scope and any specific constraints in the Guide for Authors and thematic fields when deciding to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes for positively evaluated preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints positively evaluated by PCI Mathematical and Computational Biology are publicly recommended and can be published directly in Peer Community Journal (an open‑access, indexed, generalist journal, free for authors and readers) or can be submitted to PCI-friendly journals or other journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A positive recommendation publicly posts the recommendation; authors may choose to have the recommended preprint published in Peer Community Journal or to submit it elsewhere (including journals on the PCI-friendly list). Authors should consult links provided for details about publication options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright / licensing policy for texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of comments, reviews and recommendations retain copyright © under CC-BY for texts published after and including 24/01/2022 and under CC-BY-ND before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors/reviewers/recommenders should be aware of and accept the stated licensing regime for texts published on PCI (CC-BY for material from 24/01/2022 onward; CC-BY-ND for earlier publications). Check the site for further details or changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to participate as reviewer or recommender (procedural expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: To indicate willingness to review manuscripts, users should create an account (Sign Up under Log In). To become a recommender, the site instructs: 'If you want to become a recommender send us an Email at contact@mcb.peercommunityin.org.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested community members should register an account to be available as reviewers and follow the separate Guide for Reviewers / Guide for Recommenders for eligibility, roles, and responsibilities. Becoming a recommender additionally requires contacting the editorial team as instructed.
